clue.text: A national figure -—- but Iranian Union leader taken out and whipped

indicators.note: taken out says a letter leaves the pool of 'but Iranian', and whipped (beaten into a new shape) says the rest is rearranged
a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of Union is used

explanation.surface: A patriotic figure is contrasted with an Iranian union boss who is removed from office and flogged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out and whipped' removes U (the leader of Union) from BUTIRANIAN and rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The helmeted woman with trident and shield is Britain's personified emblem, a figure seen on old coins.

clue.text: Sheridan's school subject

parts.note: reads like a lesson taught at a school run by Sheridan, but points to the title of his comedy about a school for gossip and disgrace

explanation.surface: What was taught at the school Sheridan attended?
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Brinsley Sheridan, the 18th-century playwright, wrote The School for Scandal, so the subject of his 'school' is scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: The play's title names a school devoted to gossip and disgrace, so that is what it teaches.

clue.text: Gloomy despite having heavenly body and being trendy — end life

parts.note: Saturn is a planet, a heavenly body
in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of life

explanation.surface: Someone stays gloomy even with a star body and fashionable looks, right to the end of their life.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a dark, brooding temperament, once blamed on the planet's influence.

clue.text: Body heading for grave? It's where water enters the pump

definitions.text: It's where water enters the pump

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so the opening letter of Body is taken

parts.note: a grave is the last hole anyone ends up in

explanation.surface: A corpse on its way to the cemetery, then a plumbing question about a pump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' gives B from Body; the question mark flags the playful reading of a grave as one's 'last hole'.
explanation.definitionFit: In old pump terminology the blast-hole is the opening at the bottom through which water is drawn in.

clue.text: Obtains money by extortion from key city

parts.note: B is one of the musical keys
Leeds is a city in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone squeezes cash out of a key city by threats.
explanation.walkthrough: LEEDS is a large city in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleed someone is the idiom for draining them of money, as by blackmail.

clue.text: Moon goddess retains primitive instincts -— of a non-metallic nature

indicators.note: something that retains another holds it inside, so the goddess's name wraps the instincts

parts.note: Selene is the Greek goddess of the moon
the id is Freud's term for the primitive instinctive part of the mind

explanation.surface: A moon goddess keeps hold of her primal urges, which are anything but metallic.
explanation.definitionFit: A selenide is a compound of selenium, a non-metal element, so it is of non-metallic character.

clue.text: Race for third-rate actor with a nervous affliction

parts.note: a ham is a poor, overacting performer
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A poor actor with a nervous twitch enters a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamitic is an old term for a group of North African peoples, supposedly descended from Ham; here a race of people, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The term once named a supposed ethnic and language group of North and East Africa, a people or stock.

clue.text: Glum, row up the creek to get bait

indicators.note: being up the creek means in trouble or in a mess, so the letters of 'Glum, row' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A glum angler rows up a creek in search of bait.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing marine worm, dug from sandy shores, is a favourite bait of sea anglers.

clue.text: Islet comprised entirely of granite?

parts.note: granite is a kind of rock
all means wholly or entirely

explanation.surface: A small island is wondered to be made entirely of granite.
explanation.walkthrough: Rockall is a tiny granite islet in the North Atlantic, disputed between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an isolated rocky outcrop far out in the Atlantic, a tiny island.

clue.text: Lump, when massaged with time, gets down

indicators.note: massaging kneads a thing into a new shape, so the letters of Lump are reworked

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A lump, rubbed over time, eventually goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'massaged' turns LUMP into PLUM; 'down' looks like a verb but is the soft feathers of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the soft feathering of a bird, part of its feathery covering.

clue.text: Shirt on cert provides drastic cut

parts.note: a T is short for a T-shirt
a cert is a certainty, a sure thing

explanation.surface: Betting the shirt on a racing certainty proves a severe financial blow.
explanation.walkthrough: Betting slang: putting one's shirt on a cert means staking everything on a sure winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaving of a monk's crown, about as drastic as a haircut gets.

clue.text: Doom forecast for the mother country

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A gloomy prediction is made for the motherland.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is condemnation to eternal punishment, the ultimate fate or doom.

clue.text: Overcoming despair, kept looking upwards

indicators.note: overcoming suggests the letters of despair are overturned and set in a new order

explanation.surface: Getting over despair, someone kept their eyes raised.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's sights on something higher, to hope and strive upward.

clue.text: Order snood to be put round a head

indicators.note: the net is put round the next letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a snood is a hair net
a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fit a hairnet round their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness means tidiness, a state of good order.

clue.text: Last month, a politician seen to abscond

parts.note: Dec is the standard abbreviation for December, the year's final month
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Last month an MP was seen running off with the funds.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, to run away.

clue.text: Collapses — could be the fish course!

indicators.note: could be says the letters of collapses may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A dinner falls apart at the fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: Escallops are scallops, shellfish served as a seafood dish at dinner.

clue.text: Man with driver seen to overshoot green, unfortunately

parts.note: to pass something is to go beyond or overshoot it

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of green have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer with his driver is seen to hit past the green, unluckily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' makes ENGER from GREEN. The golf picture misleads: the driver is a chauffeur, not a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is a person carried in a vehicle that someone else drives.

clue.text: Naturally, living at home dressed in a vest

indicators.note: dressed means prepared or arranged, so the letters of 'in a vest' are set in new order

explanation.surface: Someone at ease at home wears just a vest.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives are people born somewhere and living in their own country, belonging there by birth.

clue.text: Devoted little daughter following the case

indicators.note: following places the daughter's letter after the case

parts.note: an attache is a slim briefcase, the attache case
D is the short form of daughter

explanation.surface: A devoted little girl trails behind a briefcase.
explanation.definitionFit: To be attached to someone is to be fond of and loyal to them.

clue.text: Charm the stubborn with tactful introduction

parts.note: the stubborn one is a mule, proverbially obstinate

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so the opening letter of tactful is used

explanation.surface: One tries to win over an obstinate person with a diplomatic opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' reads as a verb to win over, but is a noun: a lucky trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off harm, a protective talisman.

clue.text: Hormone treatment for this bird

indicators.note: treatment means the letters of hormone are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird is given hormone therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: The moorhen is a common waterbird of ponds and rivers.

clue.text: Run! Goal! can lead to exhaustion

indicators.note: can lead to says the letters of 'Run! Goal!' produce, once rearranged, a new word

explanation.surface: A football cry urging a sprint and a score ends in tiredness.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is weariness and lack of energy, a tired listlessness.

clue.text: Why, we hear, so much is pulped to become this in the stomach

indicators.note: pulped means mashed up, so the letters are reduced and re-formed
we hear says the word Why is taken as it sounds when spoken, a single letter

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Y

explanation.surface: Someone asks why so much food is mashed up in the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns Why into Y, which joins SO MUCH to be rearranged by 'pulped'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chyme is the semi-liquid mass of partly digested food in the stomach; chymous means of that pulpy mass.

clue.text: Hear case involving listeners' complaints

indicators.note: involving here means entangling, so the letters of 'Hear case' are mixed together

explanation.surface: A court hears a case about complaints from listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture misleads: listeners are ears, and their complaints are pains.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear pain is an ailment of the organs of hearing, so a listener's complaint.

clue.text: Since I must have a brief reply they are not Europeans

parts.note: as can mean since or because
ans is the abbreviation of answer, a reply

explanation.surface: Someone insists on a short answer about who is not European.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Asia belong to a different continent from Europe.

clue.text: Drawback in English hills moving this way

indicators.note: in places the turned draw inside the hills

parts.note: the Downs are chalk hills in southern England
read as 'draw back', the word draw written backwards

explanation.surface: A setback in the English hills while heading in some direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' is read as two words: DRAW turned back gives WARD. The Downs are ranges of chalk hills in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Downwards describes movement toward lower ground, as with a down entry in a grid.

clue.text: One mill out of order is a bad sign

indicators.note: out of order means not in the right sequence, so the letters of 'One mill' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken-down mill is taken as a bad sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen of ill is a portent of bad fortune, a gloomy sign.

clue.text: Birds making throaty noises around crown of hill

indicators.note: the coughs go around the hill's top letter, holding it inside

parts.note: coughs are rough noises from the throat

indicators.note: the crown is the top, so the opening letter of hill is used

explanation.surface: Birds make croaking sounds around the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Choughs are red-billed crows of the cliffs and mountains.

clue.text: God of astronomical interest

definitions.meaning: the Roman deity of the sea
the eighth planet from the sun, studied by astronomers

explanation.definitionFit: The Roman sea god gave his name to the outer planet, so both a deity and a celestial body.

clue.text: Unstirred by vandalising burglars

indicators.note: vandalising means wrecking, so the letters of Unstirred are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Unmoved residents are targeted by vandals and house-breakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Intruders are people who break in uninvited, as thieves do.
